The work
What does a professional home organizer do?
A professional home organizer plans and sets up the spaces in your home so they are easy to use and easy to keep in order. At Home Harmonics that means walking the home with you, editing what stays, designing a system for each space, sourcing and installing the products, labeling, and handing over a care guide.
What is move-in concierge service?
Move-in concierge is a complete setup of your new home around your move: a room-by-room plan before the truck arrives, then unpacking and setting up the kitchen, pantry, closets, kids’ spaces, linens and baths, with sourcing, labeling and removal of boxes. You walk into a home that is ready to live in.
What is included in unpacking and home setup?
A plan for where everything will live, unpacking room by room, and setting up the kitchen, pantry, closets, linens, baths and kids’ spaces. Storage products are sourced and installed, everything is labeled, and boxes and packing materials are cleared away. Every engagement ends with a care guide and a check-in thirty days later.
How long does whole-home organization take?
It depends on the size of the home and how much needs editing. Whole-home work is scheduled as consecutive days, beginning at a two-day minimum, rather than spread across weeks. Your proposal sets the exact dates after the walkthrough, so you know the schedule before any work starts.
Can an organizer work with my interior designer?
Yes. Yaz works alongside interior designers, architects and builders, usually once installation is complete: organizing new cabinetry and closets, completing the move-in, and handing the home to the client ready to live in. The handoff is co-branded by default, and nothing is photographed without written consent.
Can a professional organizer prepare a custom home before move-in?
Yes. For new builds and renovations the plan starts before handover: cabinetry and closets are measured, products are specified to fit, and they are sourced in advance. On move-in, everything is unpacked into a system already designed for the space. Built storage, such as garage systems, can be arranged through a build partner.
What happens during a consultation?
First, a complimentary 15-minute fit call about what you need and when. Then a complimentary 30–45 minute walkthrough, in your home or by video, covering every space in scope, how your household uses it, and your timeline. A written proposal follows within about two business days.
How does professional organization differ from housekeeping?
Housekeeping cleans surfaces on a schedule. Organization decides where everything belongs and builds the system that keeps it there: editing, planning each space, sourcing and installing products, and labeling. Once a home is organized, cleaning is faster, because every item has a place to return to.
Can household organization be maintained after the initial project?
Yes. Every project ends with a care guide written for your household and a check-in thirty days later. Seasonal Resets, offered to every project client, bring Yaz back for wardrobe changeovers, pantry resets, holiday resets and post-travel resets, so the system keeps working as life changes.
How does a professional organize a custom closet?
By starting with the person, not the products. Yaz edits the wardrobe with you, then plans zones for what you wear most, what is seasonal and what needs care, sizes hangers and inserts to the cabinetry, and labels anything stored out of reach. The result is a closet you can see at a glance.
How do you organize a pantry?
Edit first: expired and duplicate items go. Then group food by how it is used, with daily items at eye level and occasional ones higher or lower. Decant staples into labeled canisters where it helps, use baskets for loose items, and keep a restocking guide so the system survives the next shop.
How often should an organized home be reset?
Resets usually follow the year’s natural changes: a wardrobe changeover in spring and autumn, a pantry reset, a holiday reset, or a reset after travel. You choose the rhythm. Because the system already exists, a reset restores and adjusts it rather than starting again.
Investment
How much does whole-home organization cost?
Whole-home organization with Home Harmonics begins at $1,200, which covers two full days on site. The final figure depends on the size of the home, the number of spaces, your timeline and the products chosen. You receive a fixed proposal after a complimentary walkthrough, and products are billed at cost plus a handling fee.
Do you charge by the hour?
No. Engagements are priced by project, not by the hour, so you know the investment before work begins. Single spaces begin at $600 for one full day, whole-home organization at $1,200 and move-in concierge at $1,800. A 50% deposit holds your dates.
How are products and supplies billed?
Yaz selects and purchases the products in your approved design plan, so you never have to shop or manage deliveries. Products are billed at cost plus a handling fee, within the product budget you approve in the design plan.
Can you design built-in storage, like cabinetry or a garage system?
Yes. When a space needs built storage, Yaz designs it as part of the plan and coordinates a build partner to make and install it. You see an image of the finished space before anything is built, the build is quoted separately and transparently, and Yaz organizes everything once it is installed.
Travel
Do professional organizers travel?
Home Harmonics is based in Dallas–Fort Worth and travels to clients across Texas and beyond, by arrangement. Travel engagements require a minimum of 2 on-site days, with travel and lodging billed at cost. Planning starts with a video walkthrough, so the days on site are used well.
Recent travel work includes homes across Texas and in Colorado Springs.
Can I hire an organizer for my second home?
Yes. A second home is set up much like a move-in: planned by video first, then completed in a scheduled block of on-site days, with travel and lodging at cost if it is outside Dallas–Fort Worth. A care guide makes it easy for anyone opening the house to keep it in order.
Do you work outside Dallas?
Yes. Dallas–Fort Worth is home base, and Yaz works across Texas and beyond by arrangement. Outside Dallas–Fort Worth, engagements are planned by video first and completed in a block of at least 2 on-site days, with travel and lodging billed at cost.
Privacy and people
Who will be in my home?
Yaz. Home Harmonics is led by one accountable person, so the person at your walkthrough is the person doing the work. When a project calls for built storage, such as cabinetry or garage systems, Yaz coordinates a build partner and organizes once the installation is complete.
Is my home kept private?
Client privacy is fundamental to our work. Nothing in your home is photographed or shared without your written consent, and project details are not discussed with others. Every project photograph on this site is shared with the client’s written permission.

Organizing inside custom cabinetry
Journal · 2 min readOrganizing inside custom cabinetry
Written byYaz Scott
, Founder
PublishedOctober 6, 2026
Last reviewedOctober 6, 2026
RelatedCloset & Wardrobe Organization
In short
Custom cabinetry is only as useful as what goes inside it. Organizing it well means measuring every drawer and shelf, placing items by how often they are used, and choosing inserts, risers and dividers sized to the millwork, so nothing slides, stacks or disappears behind a door.
Start with use, not products
The temptation with new cabinetry is to buy matching containers and fill the shelves. The better order is the reverse: first decide what lives in each run of cabinetry and how often it is reached for, then choose what holds it.
One rule guides most of it:
Daily: between waist and eye height, at the front, with nothing in the way.
Weekly: just above or below that zone.
Occasional: the top shelves, the deepest corners, the back of the run.
Measure everything
Interior dimensions are rarely the dimensions on the drawing. Before choosing any insert, measure:
the clear interior width, depth and height of each drawer, allowing for the slides;
the shelf spacing, and whether the shelves adjust;
hinge and door clearance, which takes space at the front of a cabinet;
anything fixed inside, such as plumbing, outlets or lighting.
An insert that is a few millimeters too wide is a drawer that will not close.
Drawers
Drawers do the most work in a well-organized kitchen or dressing room. Shallow drawers suit flat things such as cutlery, utensils, jewelry and accessories, with dividers so each piece keeps its place. Deep drawers suit pots, lids and boards stored on edge, so any one of them can be lifted out without unstacking the rest.
Shelves
Set shelf heights to the contents rather than spacing them evenly. Risers double the usable space for plates and glasses. Turntables and pull-outs bring the back of a deep cabinet forward. Anything that has to be stacked more than a few items high usually belongs somewhere else.
Pantry cabinets and tall pull-outs
Decant staples into clear, labeled canisters where it helps you see what is running low, and keep items that are used and replaced quickly in their packaging, grouped in a basket. Keep the heaviest things low and the everyday ones at eye level.
Closet millwork
In a dressing room, the ratio of long hanging to double hanging should follow the wardrobe, not the drawing, so count dresses, coats and trousers before deciding. Shoes read best on shelves where each pair is visible. Accessories belong in shallow drawers with lined dividers, where watches, belts and jewelry stay separate and easy to see.
Labels that stay quiet
Labels should help without shouting: small, consistent, and placed on shelf edges or inside drawer fronts rather than across the face of every container. In a beautiful room, the label should be the last thing you notice and the first thing you can read.
Keeping it that way
Cabinetry stays organized when everyone in the household knows where things go. A care guide records the system, and a Seasonal Reset
restores it after the holidays or a change of season.
If your cabinetry is still on the drawing board, Home Harmonics can plan the interior before it is built, and show you an image of the finished space first. If it is already installed, closet and wardrobe
and pantry and kitchen
organization begin with a complimentary walkthrough.

Journal · 3 min readWhat a move-in concierge actually does
Written byYaz Scott

In short
A move-in concierge plans and sets up your new home around your move, so you arrive to a home that already works. The work starts before moving day with a room-by-room plan, continues with unpacking and setup of every key space, and ends with the boxes gone, everything labeled and a care guide in hand.
Before the move
The work starts weeks before the truck does. A move-in concierge walks the new home, or studies the floor plan and photographs if you are relocating, and decides where each part of your household will live: which cabinet holds the everyday plates, which closet takes the linens, where the school things go.
That plan becomes three practical things:
A room-by-room map that tells the movers which room each box belongs in.
A sourcing list of drawer inserts, shelf risers, hangers and canisters, measured to the new cabinetry and ordered to arrive before you do.
A packing note for whoever is packing the old home, so boxes are labeled by destination and priority rather than “kitchen, misc.”
If you are building or renovating, this is also the moment to influence what goes inside the cabinetry: shelf heights, drawer dividers, hanging lengths in the closets. Changes on paper are easy. Changes after installation are not.
Move day
On move day the work happens in a deliberate order, so the house becomes livable as quickly as possible:
The kitchen, so the household can make coffee and eat.
Bedrooms and bathrooms, so everyone can sleep and get ready the next morning.
Children’s rooms, so the first night feels familiar.
Closets, linens and the pantry, set up to the plan rather than filled at random.
Everything is unpacked straight into its planned place and labeled where labels help. Nothing is unpacked “for now.”
The day after
The last stage is the difference between unpacked and arrived. Boxes and packing materials are broken down and removed. Each space is walked through with you, so you know where things are and why. You receive a care guide written for your household, and a check-in is booked for thirty days later, once you have lived with the system and know what to adjust.
What it is not
A move-in concierge works alongside your movers rather than replacing them. The moving company transports and places the furniture; the concierge plans, unpacks, sources, installs and labels. It is also not a one-day tidy-up. Most of the value is in the planning that happens before anything arrives.
How long it takes
It depends on the size of the home and how much is moving. Home Harmonics schedules move-ins as consecutive days, beginning at three full days on site, and sets the exact dates in a written proposal after a walkthrough. If you have a closing or move date, that date shapes the plan from the start.
When it is worth it
Relocations, when you arrive in a city where you do not yet know where anything is.
New builds and renovations, when the cabinetry is new and nothing has a place yet.
Families with young children, when the first nights need to feel normal.
Tight timelines, when a closing date or a new job leaves no room for weeks of boxes.
Questions to ask any move-in provider
Who will actually be in my home, and is it the person I spoke with?
How do you plan before moving day, and what do you need from me?
How are products sourced and billed?
What happens to the boxes and packing materials?
Will anything in my home be photographed, and with what consent?
Home Harmonics answers each of those in writing before a move begins. Move-In Concierge
starts with a complimentary walkthrough, in person or by video if you are relocating.

Journal · 2 min readHow a professional organizer works with your interior designer
Written byYaz Scott
, Founder
PublishedOctober 6, 2026

RelatedWhole-Home Organization
In short
A professional organizer works alongside your interior designer to set up what goes inside the cabinetry, closets and pantry, so the home works as well as it looks. The best results come when the organizer joins before the millwork is finalized, while shelf heights and drawer layouts can still change.
Two roles that meet at the cabinet door
An interior designer decides how a home looks and feels: the materials, the proportions, the light. An organizer decides how it works day to day: which drawer holds what, how the household moves through the kitchen in the morning, where the overflow goes. The two meet at every cabinet door, closet rod and pantry shelf.
When those decisions are made separately, the result is familiar. Beautiful millwork with shelves at the wrong height. A dressing room with too little long hanging. A pantry that cannot hold a week’s shopping.
When to bring an organizer in
The most useful moment is during the cabinetry and closet drawings, before they go to the fabricator. At that stage an organizer can:
Count what the household owns in the categories that matter, such as shoes, suits and dresses, linens, serving pieces and pantry staples, so storage is sized to real quantities.
Plan zones by frequency of use, so everyday items sit between waist and eye height and occasional ones go higher or lower.
Specify the interior fittings, such as drawer dividers, pull-outs, shelf heights and the ratio of long to double hanging, so the inside of the cabinetry is designed rather than filled.
If the millwork is already installed, a great deal can still be done with inserts, risers and adjustable shelves. There is simply more freedom on paper.
What the designer keeps
The designer keeps the vision. Organizing products should disappear into the design: matching hangers, quiet canisters, inserts in finishes that suit the cabinetry, labels that are small and consistent. Nothing should look as if it came from a different house.
A handover, done together
At the end of the project, the organizer unpacks and sets up the home, labels where it helps, and walks the client through it with a care guide written for the household. At Home Harmonics the handoff is co-branded by default, so the client receives the design and the function as one finished piece of work. White-label is available when a studio prefers it.
For homeowners
If you are working with a designer, ask whether an organizer can review the closet and cabinetry drawings before they are finalized. Small changes at that stage prevent expensive ones later. If your designer has no one in mind, Home Harmonics is glad to introduce itself.
For designers, architects and builders
Home Harmonics works with the trade on post-install organization, move-in completion and client handoff in Dallas–Fort Worth and, by arrangement, on projects elsewhere. When a project needs built storage, Yaz can design it and coordinate a build partner, with an image of the finished space before anything is made. See how trade partnerships work

Where we work
Where we workBased in Dallas. Working where you are.
Home Harmonics is based in Dallas–Fort Worth and travels to homes across Texas and beyond, by arrangement.
01Home base: Dallas–Fort Worth
Dallas, Fort Worth and the cities between. Walkthroughs in person, and engagements scheduled as consecutive days.
02Across Texas
Austin, Houston, San Antonio and anywhere in the state. Planning starts by video; the days on site are scheduled as one block.
03Beyond Texas
By arrangement, with the same model: plan by video, then a scheduled block on site. Recent work includes Colorado Springs.
Travel engagements
Planned from afar, finished in person.
Travel engagements require a minimum of 2 on-site days. Travel and lodging are billed at cost, and a 50% deposit holds the dates. Currently scheduling about 4–6 weeks out.
01Listen, by video
A virtual walkthrough of the home and the household, so the plan and sourcing are ready before arrival.
02A block on site
A scoped residency of consecutive days, with a minimum of 2 on-site days.
03Follow-up from afar
Remote follow-up, a care guide for the household, and a check-in thirty days later.
Questions
About travel.
Do professional organizers travel?
Home Harmonics is based in Dallas–Fort Worth and travels to clients across Texas and beyond, by arrangement. Travel engagements require a minimum of 2 on-site days, with travel and lodging billed at cost. Planning starts with a video walkthrough, so the days on site are used well.
Recent travel work includes homes across Texas and in Colorado Springs.
Do you work outside Dallas?
Yes. Dallas–Fort Worth is home base, and Yaz works across Texas and beyond by arrangement. Outside Dallas–Fort Worth, engagements are planned by video first and completed in a block of at least 2 on-site days, with travel and lodging billed at cost.
Can I hire an organizer for my second home?
Yes. A second home is set up much like a move-in: planned by video first, then completed in a scheduled block of on-site days, with travel and lodging at cost if it is outside Dallas–Fort Worth. A care guide makes it easy for anyone opening the house to keep it in order.
